# Job Search Tracker: Handoff

## How we're working
**Claude Code builds this; Ryan directs and reviews.** Ryan is deliberately practicing the AI-assisted development workflow many teams now use, so the process matters as much as the result.
- **Plan before building.** Propose an approach for each milestone and wait for Ryan's go-ahead.
- **Small, reviewable changes.** One milestone or feature at a time, with a short summary of what changed and why.
- **Tests alongside code.** Ryan has a QA background and will read the tests closely.
- **Explain decisions,** especially anything non-obvious about architecture or libraries. Ryan should be able to defend every choice.
- **Flag tradeoffs instead of silently picking.** Ryan prefers reasonable judgment calls on small things, so only ask about choices that matter.
- Ryan may bring in Claude Code skills he's found; follow them where they apply.

## Goal
A job search tracker that lives in the browser and goes beyond the bare status pipelines job sites offer: free-form notes, contacts, interview history, and your own assessment of fit. Built for Ryan first, but usable by anyone.

## Platform
- **Web app, local-first:** all data stored in the user's browser (IndexedDB), no server, no account
- **Installable** as a PWA so it behaves like a desktop app
- **Export and import** (JSON for full backups, CSV for spreadsheets) are required in v1, since local data can be lost if browser storage is cleared
- Cloud sync is out of scope

## Data model

### Company
Name, industry, company summary, website, dealbreaker flags (e.g., business model built on monetizing user data), notes

### Role (a job posting)
- Linked company
- Title
- Status
- Location
- Work arrangement: on-site / hybrid / remote
- Posted salary range
- Expected salary (yours)
- Job summary
- Posting link
- Posting date
- Fit for me (free text, plus an optional quick rating)
- Referral: who, and whether submitted
- Process flags (e.g., application portal you won't use)
- Next action and next action date
- Notes

### Contact
Name, role/title, company, how you know them, email/LinkedIn, notes. Linkable to a company and to specific roles (referrer, recruiter, interviewer).

### Interview
Linked role, date and time, type (recruiter screen, hiring manager, technical, panel, other), interviewers (contacts), notes, follow-up sent (yes/no)

### Status history
Auto-logged on every status change: from, to, timestamp. Never manually entered.

### Saved search
Name, link, site, last checked date

### Statuses (configurable list, sensible defaults)
Interested, Applied, Recruiter Screen, Interviewing, Offer, Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Passed

## Views
- **Pipeline board:** Kanban columns by status, drag to change status (logs history)
- **Table view:** sortable and filterable by status, company, arrangement, posting date
- **Role detail:** all fields, linked contacts, interviews, status history timeline, notes
- **Company detail:** all roles at that company, contacts, notes
- **Saved searches:** list of links with a "mark checked" button

## Daily pacing
- A gentle indicator of applications submitted today against a configurable daily target (default 2)
- Tone is encouraging, never guilt-inducing: "2 of 2 today, nice work" and nothing shown as a failure

## Import from existing tracker
Ryan has been using a spreadsheet with these columns: company, location, work arrangement, salary range, company summary, job summary, fit for him, hiring site link, hiring manager/contact, application status. Support a CSV import that maps these into the data model so he can switch over without retyping.

## AI autofill (v2, polish)
- **v2a:** paste a job posting's text, send it to the Claude API with a defined schema, and pre-fill the role and company forms. The user always reviews before saving; nothing auto-saves.
- **API key:** user brings their own, stored locally, with a clear note about cost. AI features are optional; the app works fully without them.
- **v2b (stretch):** a small browser extension with a "clip this job" button
- Avoid scraping job sites directly; pasting is more reliable and avoids terms-of-service problems.

## Milestones
1. Project setup: framework, test runner, linting, CI on every push
2. Data model and local storage layer, with unit tests (including status history logging)
3. Role and company create/edit/view
4. Table view with sorting and filtering
5. Pipeline board with drag-to-change-status
6. Contacts and interviews
7. Export/import (JSON backup, CSV export, CSV import from Ryan's spreadsheet)
8. Saved searches and daily pacing indicator
9. PWA install support
10. v2: AI autofill

## Engineering expectations
- Data layer fully unit tested: status history, linking, import/export round-trips (export then import yields identical data)
- Plain-language scenario tests for key flows, e.g. "Given a role in Applied, when it's dragged to Recruiter Screen, then a history entry is recorded with a timestamp"
- Accessibility basics: keyboard navigable, readable contrast, comfortable font sizes (Ryan finds small text hard to read; nothing below about 14px in the UI)
- Works well on desktop first; usable on a phone
- README with setup, features, and how data is stored

## Open decisions for Ryan
- Framework (Claude Code should propose one or two options with tradeoffs)
- App name
- Whether to host it publicly (e.g., GitHub Pages) so others can use it
- Rating scale for fit, if any

## Out of scope for v1
- Accounts, servers, cloud sync
- AI features (v2)
- Calendar integration
- Email integration
